# The Black Death

## The plague

The Black Death was a plague pandemic that reached Europe in 1347. It is thought to have spread along trade routes, carried by fleas that lived on rats. Historians estimate that it killed between one third and one half of the population of Europe. Contemporaries did not understand the cause and blamed bad air, divine punishment and sometimes minority groups.

## Aftermath

Labour became scarce after so many deaths, so surviving workers could demand higher wages. Landowners in many regions tried to hold wages down by law. In England these wage laws did not succeed in stopping wages from rising.
